title: Recommending the right academic programs: an interest mining approach using BERTopic
read_from: arXiv preprint 2501.06581 (published version: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery)
task: Recommending university programs from interest topics mined from course descriptions
problem: Matching personal interests to programs is hard given large, complex course catalogues; existing recommenders rely on student records.
architecture: BERTopic over course descriptions (sentence-transformer embeddings, dimensionality reduction, clustering, keyword topics); students select interest topics; programs ranked by statistical backtracking through a program-course 'knowledge map' (bi-modal network linking courses to programs).
llm_or_encoder: Sentence-Transformers models available in BERTopic (all-MiniLM-L6-v2; paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2)

datasets.name: Course descriptions (case study)
datasets.details: post-secondary institution with 80 programs and over 5,000 courses

key_results: Over 98% of surveyed users said recommendations matched their interests; about 94% would use the tool again.
Configuration reaching 98% program coverage with personalization score 0.77.
strengths: Uses only public course data, no confidential student information.
Evaluated with real users and fairness-oriented coverage analysis.

limitations.text: Depends on well-written, accurate course descriptions; one institution.
No comparison with other topic models or recommenders; topic quality not measured with coherence or diversity.
